docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This pipeline handles ingestion, transformation, and storage of DLD property data from multiple sources into MongoDB collections.

The key components include:

  • Source Data Preparation: Downloading CSV source files from URLs and uploading them to S3.
  • DLD Projects Update: Cleaning, transforming, merging projects data, and saving with archiving logic.
  • DLD Property Details Update: Processing units, lands, and buildings datasets, merging with projects, mapping location data, and saving combined property details.
  • Location Mapping: Mapping location metadata via project numbers and fallback composite keys.
  • MongoDB Management: Efficient data insertion using temporary collections, atomic renames, and index management.

docs.title: Location Mapping
docs.text: This module handles the standardization and enrichment of location data for Dubai Land Department (DLD) listings by applying a multi-step mapping process. It combines raw property and transaction data with curated mapping files and MongoDB records to produce clean, consistent location labels in the prop-ai naming format.

docs.title: Key Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Load DLD transactions, rent contracts, and multiple mapping files from S3.
  • Clean and preprocess raw location fields from DLD source data.
  • Apply mapping logic using:
  • Project number
  • Exact multi-field matches
  • Single field fallback matches
  • Enrich records with hierarchical labels: building, project, master project, area.
  • Generate structured mapping keys and classification flags.
  • Log anomalies and missing mappings (e.g. unmatched master_project_en).
  • Persist results to both CSV and MongoDB collections.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• A fully mapped and classified DataFrame with enriched prop-ai fields.
  • Optional hierarchical records to supplement project and area hierarchy.
  • Saved outputs in both .csv format and MongoDB collections.

This pipeline ensures consistent and hierarchical geolocation data across DLD sources, which is crucial for search, filtering, reporting, and property aggregation logic.

def clean_text_columns(df, columns, placeholder=""):
    """
    Clean and standardize specified text columns in a DataFrame.

    This function uppercases, trims leading/trailing whitespace, replaces multiple spaces with a 
    single space, and replaces instances of `' , '` with `', '` for all specified text columns. 
    It also replaces `NaN` and empty strings with a placeholder value.

    Args:
        df (pd.DataFrame): The input DataFrame.
        columns (list[str]): List of column names to clean.
        placeholder (str, optional): Value to replace `NaN` and empty strings. Defaults to `""`.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: The cleaned DataFrame with standardized text columns.
    """
    for col in columns:
        if df[col].dtype == "object":
            df[col] = df[col].str.upper().str.strip().str.replace(" +", " ", regex=True).str.replace(" , ", ", ", regex=False).fillna(placeholder).replace("", placeholder)
    return df

def determine_mapping_type(row):
    """
    Determine the mapping type for a row based on available fields.

    Args:
        row (pd.Series): DataFrame row.

    Returns:
        str: One of ['building', 'project', 'master_project', 'area']
    """
    if pd.notna(row['building_name_en']):
        return "building"
    elif pd.notna(row['project_name_en']):
        return "project"
    elif pd.notna(row['master_project_en']):
        return "master_project"
    else:
        return "area"

def enrich_with_labels(locations_df):
    """
    Enrich the locations DataFrame with human-readable labels by merging data from MongoDB collections.

    Args:
        locations_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame with location keys to enrich.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Enriched DataFrame with label columns merged.
    """
        # Connect to databases
    dev_client = MongoClient(os.getenv('DEV_MONGO_DB_URL'))

    dev_db = dev_client['dev_listings_db']

    # Load reference data
    projects_df = pd.DataFrame(list(dev_db['data_projects'].find()))
    master_projects_df = pd.DataFrame(list(dev_db['data_master_projects'].find()))
    areas_df = pd.DataFrame(list(dev_db['data_areas'].find()))

    # Create keys in projects_df
    projects_df['prop-ai_location_key_building'] = make_key(projects_df, [
        'area_name_prop-ai', 'master_project_prop-ai', 'project_name_prop-ai', 'building_name_prop-ai'
    ])

    projects_df['prop-ai_location_key_project'] = make_key(projects_df, [
        'area_name_prop-ai', 'master_project_prop-ai', 'project_name_prop-ai'
    ])

    # Merge building_name_label
    if 'building_name_label' in projects_df.columns:
        building_labels = projects_df[['prop-ai_location_key_building', 'building_name_label']].drop_duplicates()
        locations_df = locations_df.merge(building_labels, on='prop-ai_location_key_building', how='left')

    # Merge project_name_label
    if 'project_name_label' in projects_df.columns:
        project_labels = projects_df[['prop-ai_location_key_project', 'project_name_label']].drop_duplicates()
        locations_df = locations_df.merge(project_labels, on='prop-ai_location_key_project', how='left')

    # Create key in master_projects_df and merge master_project_label
    master_projects_df['prop-ai_location_key_masterproject'] = make_key(master_projects_df, [
        'area_name_prop-ai', 'master_project_prop-ai'
    ])

    if 'master_project_label' in master_projects_df.columns:
        master_labels = master_projects_df[['prop-ai_location_key_masterproject', 'master_project_label']].drop_duplicates()
        locations_df = locations_df.merge(master_labels, on='prop-ai_location_key_masterproject', how='left')

    # Create key in areas_df and merge area_name_label
    areas_df['prop-ai_location_key_area'] = areas_df['area_name_prop-ai'].fillna('')

    if 'area_name_label' in areas_df.columns:
        area_labels = areas_df[['prop-ai_location_key_area', 'area_name_label']].drop_duplicates()
        locations_df = locations_df.merge(area_labels, on='prop-ai_location_key_area', how='left')

    # Remove duplicate columns that may have been created during merging
    locations_df = locations_df.loc[:, ~locations_df.columns.str.endswith(('_x', '_y'))]

    return locations_df

def generate_hierarchical_records(df_combined):
    """
    Generate additional hierarchical records for projects, master projects, and areas
    based on existing mapped records.

    Args:
        df_combined (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame with mapping data.

    Returns:
        list[dict]: List of new records to append.
    """
    new_records = []

    def record_exists(df, mapping_type, area, master, project):
        return (
            (df['mapping_type'] == mapping_type) &
            (df['area_name_en'] == area) &
            (df['master_project_en'] == master) &
            (df['project_name_en'] == project)
        ).any()

    for _, row in df_combined.iterrows(): 
        # if pd.notna(row["project_number"]): 
        #     continue

        area = row['area_name_en']
        master = row['master_project_en']
        project = row['project_name_en']

        base_fields = {
            'area_name_en': area,
            'area_name_prop-ai': row['area_name_prop-ai'],
            'building_name_en': None,
            'building_name_prop-ai': None,
            'project_name_en': None,
            'project_name_prop-ai': None,
            'master_project_en': None,
            'master_project_prop-ai': None,
            'project_number': None,
            'Source': row['Source'],
            'mapped_status': True,
            'auto_update': True,
            'updated_at': pd.Timestamp.now()
        }

        if row['mapping_type'] == 'building':
            # Add project record if doesn't exist
            if not record_exists(df_combined, 'project', area, master, project):
                new_records.append({
                    **base_fields,
                    'mapping_type': 'project',
                    'project_name_en': project,
                    'project_name_prop-ai': row['project_name_prop-ai'],
                    'master_project_en': master,
                    'master_project_prop-ai': row['master_project_prop-ai'],
                })

            # Add master_project record if doesn't exist
            if not record_exists(df_combined, 'master_project', area, master, None):
                new_records.append({
                    **base_fields,
                    'mapping_type': 'master_project',
                    'master_project_en': master,
                    'master_project_prop-ai': row['master_project_prop-ai'],
                })

            # Add area record if doesn't exist
            if not record_exists(df_combined, 'area', area, None, None):
                new_records.append({
                    **base_fields,
                    'mapping_type': 'area'
                })

        elif row['mapping_type'] == 'project':
            # Add master_project record if doesn't exist
            if not record_exists(df_combined, 'master_project', area, master, None):
                new_records.append({
                    **base_fields,
                    'mapping_type': 'master_project',
                    'master_project_en': master,
                    'master_project_prop-ai': row['master_project_prop-ai'],
                })

            # Add area record if doesn't exist
            if not record_exists(df_combined, 'area', area, None, None):
                new_records.append({
                    **base_fields,
                    'mapping_type': 'area'
                })

        elif row['mapping_type'] == 'master_project':
            # Add area record if doesn't exist
            if not record_exists(df_combined, 'area', area, None, None):
                new_records.append({
                    **base_fields,
                    'mapping_type': 'area'
                })

    return new_records

def generate_location_keys(df_combined):
    """
    Generate concatenated location keys based on prop-ai naming conventions.

    Args:
        df_combined (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame containing prop-ai location fields.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: DataFrame with new location key columns added.
    """
    df_combined['prop-ai_location_key'] = (
        df_combined['area_name_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['master_project_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['project_name_prop-ai'].fillna('')
    )

    df_combined['prop-ai_location_key_building'] = (
        df_combined['area_name_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['master_project_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['project_name_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['building_name_prop-ai'].fillna('')
    )

    df_combined['prop-ai_location_key_project'] = (
        df_combined['area_name_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['master_project_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['project_name_prop-ai'].fillna('')
    )

    df_combined['prop-ai_location_key_masterproject'] = (
        df_combined['area_name_prop-ai'].fillna('') + "_" + 
        df_combined['master_project_prop-ai'].fillna('')
    )

    df_combined['prop-ai_location_key_area'] = df_combined['area_name_prop-ai'].fillna('')

    return df_combined

def load_dld_data_from_s3():
    """
    Load DLD transaction and rental contract data from S3, decompress and return as DataFrames.

    Returns:
        tuple:
            pandas.DataFrame: DLD transactions data.
            pandas.DataFrame: DLD rent contracts data.

    Raises:
        Exception: If loading from S3 or decompression fails.
    """
    s3_client = get_s3_client()
    today = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d')

    # Define S3 paths
    transactions_key = f'source_data/dld_data/{today}_dld_transactions.csv'
    rent_contracts_key = f'source_data/dld_data/{today}_dld_rent_contracts.csv'
    bucket_name = 'prop-ai-transactions'

    # Define local file paths
    local_transactions_file = f'temp_{today}_dld_transactions.csv.gz'
    local_rent_contracts_file = f'temp_{today}_dld_rent_contracts.csv.gz'

    # Load transactions
    logger.info(f"Loading DLD transactions from S3: s3://{bucket_name}/{transactions_key}")
    try:
        # Download to local file
        s3_client.download_file(bucket_name, transactions_key, local_transactions_file)

        # Load from local file
        with gzip.open(local_transactions_file, 'rt') as gz:
            df_transactions = pd.read_csv(gz)
        logger.info(f"Successfully loaded {len(df_transactions)} transaction records")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to load transactions from S3: {str(e)}")
        raise

    # Load rent contracts
    logger.info(f"Loading DLD rent contracts from S3: s3://{bucket_name}/{rent_contracts_key}")
    try:
        # Download to local file
        s3_client.download_file(bucket_name, rent_contracts_key, local_rent_contracts_file)

        # Load from local file
        with gzip.open(local_rent_contracts_file, 'rt') as gz:
            df_rent_contracts = pd.read_csv(gz)
        logger.info(f"Successfully loaded {len(df_rent_contracts)} rent contract records")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to load rent contracts from S3: {str(e)}")
        raise

    # Clean up local files
    try:
        if os.path.exists(local_transactions_file):
            os.remove(local_transactions_file)
        if os.path.exists(local_rent_contracts_file):
            os.remove(local_rent_contracts_file)
        logger.info("Local temporary files cleaned up")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to clean up temporary files: {str(e)}")

    # Filter to required fields
    required_fields = [
        'area_name_en', 'master_project_en', 'project_name_en', 'building_name_en', 'project_number',
        'area_name_prop-ai', 'master_project_prop-ai', 'project_name_prop-ai', 'building_name_prop-ai'
    ]

    # Keep only required fields that exist in the dataframes
    transactions_fields = [field for field in required_fields if field in df_transactions.columns]
    rent_contracts_fields = [field for field in required_fields if field in df_rent_contracts.columns]

    df_transactions = df_transactions[transactions_fields]
    df_rent_contracts = df_rent_contracts[rent_contracts_fields]

    df_rent_contracts["building_name_en"] = ""

    return df_transactions, df_rent_contracts

def load_mapping_files():
    """
    Load mapping CSV files from S3 into pandas DataFrames.

    Returns:
        dict: Dictionary mapping file keys to pandas DataFrames.

    Raises:
        Exception: If loading any file from S3 fails.
    """
    s3_client = get_s3_client()
    bucket_name = 'prop-ai-source-files'

    mapping_files = {
        'data_areas': "dubai_data_projects/data_areas.csv",
        'data_master_projects': "dubai_data_projects/data_master_projects.csv",
        'data_projects': "dubai_data_projects/data_projects.csv",
        'data_buildings': "dubai_data_projects/data_buildings.csv",
    }

    mapping_sheets = {}

    for key, file_path in mapping_files.items():
        try:
            logger.info(f"Loading mapping file from S3: s3://{bucket_name}/{file_path}")
            obj = s3_client.get_object(Bucket=bucket_name, Key=file_path)
            csv_data = obj['Body'].read().decode('utf-8')
            mapping_sheets[key] = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv_data))
            mapping_sheets[key] = mapping_sheets[key].applymap(clean_value)
            logger.info(f"Successfully loaded {key} with {len(mapping_sheets[key])} records")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to load {file_path} from S3: {str(e)}")
            raise

    return mapping_sheets

    Post-process DataFrame by generating mapping_type, filling missing prop-ai fields, and setting flags.

    Args:
        df_combined (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame after mapping steps.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Post-processed DataFrame.
    """
        # Generate mapping_type
    df_combined['mapping_type'] = df_combined.apply(determine_mapping_type, axis=1)

    # Auto-update _prop-ai fields where _en has a value but _prop-ai is null
    for field in ["project_name", "master_project", "area_name", "building_name"]:
        en_field = f"{field}_en"
        prop_ai_field = f"{field}_prop-ai"

        if en_field in df_combined.columns and prop_ai_field in df_combined.columns:
            mask = df_combined[prop_ai_field].isna() & df_combined[en_field].notna()
            df_combined.loc[mask, prop_ai_field] = df_combined.loc[mask, en_field]

    # Generate development_name_prop-ai
    def generate_development_name(row):
        parts = [row['master_project_prop-ai'], row['project_name_prop-ai']]
        return ", ".join([p for p in parts if pd.notna(p)])

    df_combined['development_name_prop-ai'] = df_combined.apply(generate_development_name, axis=1)
    empty_mask = df_combined['development_name_prop-ai'] == ""
    df_combined.loc[empty_mask, 'development_name_prop-ai'] = df_combined.loc[empty_mask, 'area_name_prop-ai']

    mask = df_combined[["project_name_prop-ai", "master_project_prop-ai", "area_name_prop-ai", "building_name_prop-ai"]].isna().any(axis=1)
    df_combined['auto_update'] = mask

def clean_projects_dataframe(df):
    """
    Clean the DLD projects dataframe by:
    - Dropping unnecessary Arabic language and description columns.
    - Converting ID columns to string and cleaning trailing decimals.
    - Uppercasing and stripping key text columns.
    - Parsing date columns to datetime objects.

    Args:
        df (pd.DataFrame): Raw projects dataframe.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Cleaned projects dataframe.
    """
    logging.info('Cleaning projects dataframe')

    # Drop unnecessary columns
    columns_to_drop = [
        'project_name', 'developer_name', 'master_developer_name',
        'project_type_ar', 'project_classification_ar', 'escrow_agent_name',
        'project_status_ar', 'project_description_ar', 'area_name_ar',
        'master_project_ar', 'zoning_authority_ar'
    ]

    df = df.drop([col for col in columns_to_drop if col in df.columns], axis=1)

    # Convert ID columns to string and clean
    id_columns = [
        'project_id', 'project_number', 'developer_id', 'developer_number',
        'master_developer_id', 'master_developer_number', 'project_type_id',
        'project_classification_id', 'escrow_agent_id', 'property_id',
        'area_id', 'zoning_authority_id'
    ]

    for col in id_columns:
        if col in df.columns:
            df[col] = df[col].astype(str)
            if col in ['developer_id', 'developer_number', 'escrow_agent_id', 'area_id']:
                df[col] = df[col].str.rstrip('.0')

    # Clean text columns
    columns_to_process = ['area_name_en', 'project_name_en', 'master_project_en']
    for col in columns_to_process:
        if col in df.columns and df[col].dtype == 'object':
            df[col] = df[col].str.upper().str.strip()

    # Convert date columns
    date_columns = ['project_start_date', 'project_end_date', 'completion_date', 'cancellation_date']
    for col in date_columns:
        if col in df.columns:
            df[col] = pd.to_datetime(df[col], dayfirst=True, format='mixed')

    return df

def dld_projects_update(db):
    """
    Process and update DLD projects data from S3 CSV to MongoDB.

    This function:
    - Loads a compressed DLD projects CSV from S3.
    - Cleans and standardizes the DataFrame.
    - Merges it with unique project numbers from transactions for validation.
    - Maps location details from a location mapping collection.
    - Saves updated projects to MongoDB with archiving for changed records.
    - Frees memory after processing.

    Args:
        db (pymongo.database.Database): The MongoDB database instance where project data will be saved.

    Raises:
        Exception: If any processing or saving step fails.
    """
    logging.info('Starting DLD projects update')

    try:
        # Read projects data
        dld_projects_df = pd.read_csv(
            f's3://{TRANSACTION_BUCKET}/source_data/dld_data/{current_date}_dld_projects.csv',
            header=0, 
            compression='gzip', 
            storage_options={"key": ACCESS_ID, "secret": ACCESS_KEY}
        )

        logging.info(f"Loaded {len(dld_projects_df)} project records")

        # Clean dataframe
        cleaned_dld_projects_df = clean_projects_dataframe(dld_projects_df)
        logging.info(f"After cleaning: {len(cleaned_dld_projects_df)} project records")

        # Get unique project numbers from transactions
        dld_transaction_df = create_dataframe_from_db_dld_transactions()
        logging.info(f"Found {len(dld_transaction_df)} unique projects in transactions")

        cleaned_dld_projects_df['project_number'] = pd.to_numeric(cleaned_dld_projects_df['project_number'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        dld_transaction_df['project_number'] = pd.to_numeric(dld_transaction_df['project_number'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

        # Merge with transactions
        cleaned_dld_projects_df = cleaned_dld_projects_df.merge(
            dld_transaction_df, on='project_number', how='left'
        )

        # Get location mapping
        dld_location_mapping_df = create_dataframe_from_db_dld_location_mapping()

    Process and update DLD property details for buildings, units, and lands.

    This function:
    - Reads compressed CSVs from S3 for each property type.
    - Adds source identifier and converts ID fields to numeric format.
    - Cleans and standardizes relevant text columns.

    - Saves individual and combined property details into MongoDB collections.
    - Performs memory cleanup after execution.

    Raises:
        Exception: If any part of the update process fails.
    """
    logging.info('Starting DLD property details update')

    try:
        # Read and clean property data
        property_data = {}
        property_types = ['buildings', 'units', 'lands']

        # Load project data
        projects_df = get_projects_for_merge(db)
        if not projects_df.empty:
            projects_df['project_id'] = pd.to_numeric(projects_df['project_id'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        else:
            logging.warning("Project data is empty. Skipping project merge.")
            projects_df = None


        for prop_type in property_types:
            df = pd.read_csv(
                f's3://{TRANSACTION_BUCKET}/source_data/dld_data/{current_date}_dld_{prop_type}.csv',
                header=0, compression='gzip',
                storage_options={"key": ACCESS_ID, "secret": ACCESS_KEY}

            df['Source_Data'] = f'dld_{prop_type}'


            # Convert property_id and project_id to numeric

            df['project_id'] = pd.to_numeric(df['project_id'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

            # Clean text columns

            for col in columns_to_process:

            # Merge with projects_df if available
            if projects_df is not None:
                duplicate_cols = [col for col in projects_df.columns if col in df.columns and col != 'project_id']

def map_location_data(projects_df, location_df):
    """
    Map location data from location_df to projects_df by:
    - Primary join on 'project_number'.
    - Fallback join on composite keys ['area_name_en', 'master_project_en', 'project_name_en'] for missing locations.

    Adds empty columns 'building_name_en' and 'building_name_prop-ai' to final DataFrame.

    Args:
        projects_df (pd.DataFrame): Projects DataFrame.
        location_df (pd.DataFrame): Location mapping DataFrame.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Projects DataFrame enriched with location mapping.
    """

    if location_df.empty:
        logging.warning("Location mapping DataFrame is empty")
        return projects_df

    logging.info('Applying location mapping')

    # Ensure proper types
    projects_df['project_number'] = pd.to_numeric(projects_df['project_number'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
    location_df['project_number'] = pd.to_numeric(location_df['project_number'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    # Drop duplicates in location_df based on project_number
    location_by_number = location_df[location_df['project_number'].notna()].drop_duplicates(subset=['project_number'])

    # Identify common columns (excluding project_number)
    common_cols = list(set(projects_df.columns) & set(location_by_number.columns)) 
    common_cols.remove('project_number')

    # Drop common columns from left (projects_df)
    projects_df = projects_df.drop(columns=common_cols, errors='ignore')

    # First merge on project_number
    merged_df = projects_df.merge(location_by_number, on='project_number', how='left')

    # SECONDARY MERGE (fallback) using composite key
    composite_keys = ['area_name_en', 'master_project_en', 'project_name_en']
    missing_locations = merged_df[merged_df['project_number'].isna()]

    # Drop common columns from left before second merge
    missing_locations = missing_locations.drop(columns=[col for col in missing_locations.columns if col in location_df.columns and col not in composite_keys], errors='ignore')
    location_by_keys = location_df.dropna(subset=composite_keys).drop_duplicates(subset=composite_keys)

    # Merge on composite keys
    merged_fallback = missing_locations.merge(location_by_keys, on=composite_keys, how='left')

    # Combine the successfully merged rows with fallback rows
    successfully_mapped = merged_df[~merged_df['area_name_en'].isna()]
    final_df = pd.concat([successfully_mapped, merged_fallback], ignore_index=True)

    final_df["building_name_en"] = None
    final_df["building_name_prop-ai"] = None

    logging.info('Location mapping completed with project_number and composite key fallback')
    return final_df

def save_projects_to_db(db, df):
    """
    Save the cleaned projects dataframe to MongoDB, maintaining an archive for updated records.

    For each project record:
    - Checks if a record with same project_number exists.
    - If exists and data changed, archive old record with timestamps.
    - Insert or update current record with updated timestamp.

    Args:
        db (pymongo.database.Database): MongoDB database handle.
        df (pd.DataFrame): Cleaned projects dataframe.
    """
    logging.info('Saving projects to database')

    primary_key = 'project_number'
    collection_name = 'dld_projects'
    archive_collection_name = 'dld_projects_archive'

    # Clear archive collection
    db[archive_collection_name].delete_many({})

    records = df.to_dict(orient='records')

    # Process date fields
    for record in records:
        for date_field in ['project_start_date', 'project_end_date', 'completion_date', 'cancellation_date']:
            if record.get(date_field):
                try:
                    if isinstance(record[date_field], str):
                        record[date_field] = datetime.strptime(record[date_field], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z')
                    elif pd.isna(record[date_field]):
                        record[date_field] = None
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    record[date_field] = None

    # Update with archiving logic
    for record in records:
        existing_document = db[collection_name].find_one({primary_key: record[primary_key]})
        if existing_document:
            # Check for updates
            has_updates = any(
                record[key] != existing_document.get(key)
                for key in record if key != 'property_id'
            )
            if has_updates:
                # Archive existing document
                existing_document['date_updated'] = datetime.now()
                existing_document.pop('_id', None)
                existing_document['archived_at'] = datetime.now()
                db[archive_collection_name].insert_one(existing_document)

                # Replace with new document
                record['date_updated'] = datetime.now()
                db[collection_name].replace_one({primary_key: record[primary_key]}, record, upsert=True)
        else:
            # Insert new record
            record['date_updated'] = datetime.now()
            db[collection_name].insert_one(record)

    logging.info(f'Saved {len(records)} projects to database')

def save_property_collection(db, df, collection_name):
    """
    Save property data to a MongoDB collection using a temporary collection swap approach.

    - Converts NaNs to None for MongoDB compatibility.
    - Clears a temporary collection and inserts all records.
    - Drops the original collection and renames the temp collection atomically.

    Args:
        db (pymongo.database.Database): MongoDB database object.
        df (pd.DataFrame): Property data to save.
        collection_name (str): Target MongoDB collection name.
    """
    logging.info(f'Saving {len(df)} records to {collection_name}')

    temp_collection_name = f'{collection_name}_temp'
    records = df.drop(columns=['_id'], errors='ignore').to_dict(orient='records')

    # Convert NaNs to None
    for record in records:
        for key, value in record.items():
            if not isinstance(value, (list, dict)) and pd.isnull(value):
                record[key] = None

    if records:
        # Drop temp collection if it exists
        db[temp_collection_name].delete_many({})  # Clear it instead of drop to avoid index loss if any

        # Insert all records
        db[temp_collection_name].insert_many(records)

        # Replace old collection
        db[collection_name].drop()
        db[temp_collection_name].rename(collection_name)

    logging.info(f'Successfully saved to {collection_name}')

def clean_and_convert_column(series, target_type):
    """
    Clean and convert a pandas Series column to a specified target type.

    Args:
        series (pandas.Series): The data column to clean and convert.
        target_type (str): The target data type. One of: 'string', 'date', 'float', 'int'.

    Returns:
        (pandas.Series): Converted and cleaned Series.

    Notes:
        - Strings "nan", "None", "null" are replaced with None for 'string' target.
        - Dates are parsed with errors coerced to NaT.
        - Numeric conversions coerce errors to NaN/nullable integers.
    """
    if target_type == "string":
        return series.astype(str).replace(["nan", "None", "null"], None)

    elif target_type == "date":
        return pd.to_datetime(series, errors="coerce")

    elif target_type == "float":
        return pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce").astype("float64")

    elif target_type == "int":
        return pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce").astype(
            "Int64"
        )  # Nullable integer

    return series

def upload_batch_to_collection(collection, records, batch_size, data_type):
    """
    Upload records to MongoDB collection in batches.

    Args:
        collection (pymongo.collection.Collection): MongoDB collection object.
        records (list of dict): List of records (documents) to insert.
        batch_size (int): Number of records to insert per batch.
        data_type (str): Descriptive name of the data type being uploaded (for logging).

    Returns:
        None
    """
    total_records = len(records)
    inserted_count = 0
    failed_batches = []

    logger.info(
        f"Starting batch upload of {total_records} {data_type} records (batch size: {batch_size})"
    )

    for i in range(0, total_records, batch_size):
        batch_num = i // batch_size + 1
        batch = records[i : i + batch_size]

        try:
            for record in batch:
                for key, value in record.items():
                    if not isinstance(value, (list, dict)) and pd.isnull(value):
                        record[key] = None

            result = collection.insert_many(batch, ordered=False)
            inserted_count += len(result.inserted_ids)

            logger.info(
                f"{data_type.capitalize()} Batch {batch_num}: Successfully inserted {len(batch)} records "
                f"({inserted_count}/{total_records} total)"
            )

        except Exception as batch_error:
            logger.error(
                f"{data_type.capitalize()} Batch {batch_num} failed: {str(batch_error)}"
            )
            failed_batches.append(batch_num)
            continue

    # Summary
    if failed_batches:
        logger.warning(
            f"{data_type.capitalize()} upload completed with errors. Failed batches: {failed_batches}"
        )
        logger.info(
            f"Successfully inserted {inserted_count}/{total_records} {data_type} records"
        )
    else:
        logger.info(
            f"✅ Successfully uploaded all {inserted_count} {data_type} records"
        )

def upload_to_mongodb(
    df_transactions, df_charges, batch_size=100000, clear_existing=True
):
    """
    Upload processed data to MongoDB.

    Args:
        df_transactions (pandas.DataFrame): Processed transactions data.
        df_charges (pandas.DataFrame): Processed service charges data.
        batch_size (int, optional): Number of records to upload per batch. Defaults to 100000.
        clear_existing (bool, optional): Whether to clear existing data before upload. Defaults to True.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If MongoDB connection URL is not configured.
        Exception: For any errors during upload.
    """
    logger.info("Uploading data to MongoDB...")

    if not DEV_MONGO_DB_URL:
        logger.error("DEV_MONGO_DB_URL not found in environment variables")
        raise ValueError("MongoDB connection URL not configured")

    client = MongoClient(DEV_MONGO_DB_URL)

    try:
        dev_db = client["dev_listings_db"]

        # Define collections (only processed data, no raw collections)
        collections = {
            "transactions": dev_db["dld_transactions_all_properties_v2"],
            "charges": dev_db["dld_service_charges"],
        }

        # Clear existing data if requested
        if clear_existing:
            logger.info("Clearing existing data...")
            for name, collection in collections.items():
                delete_result = collection.delete_many({})
                logger.info(
                    f"Deleted {delete_result.deleted_count} existing {name} records"
                )

        # Upload data
        datasets = [
            (df_transactions, collections["transactions"], "processed transactions"),
            (df_charges, collections["charges"], "processed charges"),
        ]

        for df, collection, description in datasets:
            if not df.empty:
                records = df.to_dict(orient="records")
                logger.info(f"Uploading {len(records)} {description} records...")
                upload_batch_to_collection(collection, records, batch_size, description)

        logger.info("✅ Successfully uploaded all data to MongoDB")

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"❌ Error during upload process: {str(e)}")
        raise

    finally:
        client.close()
        logger.info("MongoDB connection closed")

def calculate_resale_metrics(transactions_df):
    """
    Calculate resale metrics for property transactions.

    This includes calculating:
    - Number of times a property was sold.
    - Price change relative to the last sale.
    - Price change relative to the first sale of the property.

    Args:
        transactions_df (pandas.DataFrame): DataFrame containing property transaction records.

    Returns:
        pandas.DataFrame: Transactions DataFrame enriched with resale metrics.

    Logs:
        Number of CPU cores used for parallel processing.
        Progress of resale metrics calculation.
        Completion confirmation.
    """
    logger.info("Calculating resale metrics")

    # Preprocess
    transactions_df["instance_date"] = pd.to_datetime(transactions_df["instance_date"])
    transactions_df = transactions_df.sort_values(['property_id', 'instance_date']).reset_index(drop=True)

    def calculate_metrics_single_group(group):
        group = group.sort_values('instance_date').copy()
        group['number_times_sold'] = range(1, len(group) + 1)
        group['last_worth'] = group['actual_worth'].shift(1)
        group['price_change_vs_last_sale'] = (
            (group['actual_worth'] / group['last_worth']) - 1
        ).where(group['last_worth'].notna() & (group['last_worth'] != 0))

        try:
            first_worth = group.loc[group['sale_type_id'] == 1, 'actual_worth'].iloc[0]
            if first_worth != 0:
                group['price_change_vs_first_sale'] = (group['actual_worth'] / first_worth) - 1
            else:
                group['price_change_vs_first_sale'] = pd.NA
        except IndexError:
            group['price_change_vs_first_sale'] = pd.NA

        return group.drop(columns='last_worth')

    # Parallel processing
    grouped = list(transactions_df.groupby('property_id'))
    num_cores = multiprocessing.cpu_count()
    logger.info(f"Processing resale metrics with {num_cores} cores")

    results = Parallel(n_jobs=num_cores)(
        delayed(calculate_metrics_single_group)(group) 
        for _, group in tqdm(grouped, desc="Processing resale metrics")
    )

    # Batch concatenation
    batch_size = 2000
    batches = []
    for i in tqdm(range(0, len(results), batch_size), desc="Concatenating batches"):
        batch = pd.concat(results[i:i + batch_size], ignore_index=True)
        batches.append(batch)

    final_df = pd.concat(batches, ignore_index=True)
    logger.info("Resale metrics calculation completed")
    return final_df

    - Replace NaN values with empty strings in dicts and fields.

    """
    logger.info("Performing final data cleaning")

    def replace_nan_with_empty_string(obj):
        if pd.isna(obj):
            return ""
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            new_dict = {}
            for k, v in obj.items():
                new_k = "" if pd.isna(k) else k
                if isinstance(v, dict):
                    new_v = replace_nan_with_empty_string(v)
                elif pd.isna(v):
                    new_v = ""
                else:
                    new_v = v
                new_dict[new_k] = new_v
            return new_dict
        return obj

def create_units_and_villas(transactions_df, property_details_df):
    """
    Create dictionaries of units, villas, and lands for each transaction in the dataset.

    This function matches transactions with property details based on composite keys formed
    from project number, area, rooms, and property subtype. It separates properties into units,
    villas, and lands, and aggregates their relevant details into dictionaries attached to each transaction.

    Args:
        transactions_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of property transactions.
        property_details_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame with detailed property attributes.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: transactions_df enriched with columns:
            - 'unit_numbers'
            - 'villa_numbers'
            - 'land_numbers'
        Each containing a dictionary of relevant property details keyed by unit/building number.

    Logs:
        Info on the creation process start and successful completion.
    """
    logger.info("Creating project dictionaries")

    # Ensure unique indices to avoid reindexing errors
    transactions_df = transactions_df.reset_index(drop=True)

    property_details_df = property_details_df[~property_details_df["project_number"].isna()]

    # Convert to numeric once
    transactions_df['project_number_numeric'] = pd.to_numeric(transactions_df['project_number'], errors='coerce')
    property_details_df['project_number_numeric'] = pd.to_numeric(property_details_df['project_number'], errors='coerce')

    # Create merge keys for efficient joining
    transactions_df['merge_key'] = (
        transactions_df['project_number_numeric'].astype(str) + '_' +
        transactions_df['procedure_area'].astype(str) + '_' +
        transactions_df['rooms_en'].astype(str) + '_' +
        transactions_df['property_sub_type_en'].astype(str)
    )

    property_details_df['merge_key'] = (
        property_details_df['project_number_numeric'].astype(str) + '_' +
        property_details_df['actual_area'].astype(str) + '_' +
        property_details_df['rooms_en'].astype(str) + '_' +
        property_details_df['property_sub_type_en'].astype(str)
    )

    # Initialize result columns
    transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'] = [{}] * len(transactions_df)
    transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'] = [{}] * len(transactions_df)
    transactions_df['land_numbers_all'] = [{}] * len(transactions_df)

    # Separate property details by source type for efficiency
    unit_details = property_details_df[property_details_df['Source_Data'] == 'dld_units'].copy()
    land_details = property_details_df[property_details_df['Source_Data'] == 'dld_lands'].copy()

    # Process Units (Apartments & Hotel Apartments)
    apartment_mask = transactions_df['property_type_prop-ai'].isin(['Apartment', 'Hotel Apartment'])

    if apartment_mask.any() and not unit_details.empty:
        # Group unit details by merge_key
        unit_groups = unit_details.groupby('merge_key').apply(
            lambda group: {
                row['unit_number']: {
                    'floor': row['floor'],
                    'unit_balcony_area': row['unit_balcony_area'],
                    'unit_parking_number': row['unit_parking_number'], 
                    'rooms': row['rooms'],
                    'rooms_en': row['rooms_en'], 
                    'building_number': row['building_number'],
                    'property_type_en': row['property_type_en'], 
                    'property_sub_type_en': row['property_sub_type_en'],
                    'land_type_en': row['land_type_en'], 
                    'parcel_id': row['parcel_id'], 
                    'property_id': row['property_id']
                }
                for _, row in group.iterrows()
            }
        ).to_dict()

        # Map unit dictionaries to transactions using boolean indexing
        transactions_df.loc[apartment_mask, 'unit_numbers_all'] = (
            transactions_df.loc[apartment_mask, 'merge_key']
            .map(lambda key: unit_groups.get(key, {}))
        )

    # Process Villas
    villa_mask = transactions_df['property_type_prop-ai'] == 'Villa'

    if villa_mask.any() and not unit_details.empty:
        # Group villa details by merge_key
        villa_groups = unit_details.groupby('merge_key').apply(
            lambda group: {
                row['building_number']: {
                    'built_up_area': row['built_up_area'], 
                    'car_parks': row['car_parks'],
                    'rooms': row['rooms'], 
                    'rooms_en': row['rooms_en'], 
                    'floors': row['floors'],
                    'property_type_en': row['property_type_en'], 
                    'property_sub_type_en': row['property_sub_type_en'],
                    'land_type_en': row['land_type_en'], 
                    'parcel_id': row['parcel_id'], 
                    'property_id': row['property_id']
                }
                for _, row in group.iterrows()
            }
        ).to_dict()

        # Map villa dictionaries to transactions using boolean indexing
        transactions_df.loc[villa_mask, 'villa_numbers_all'] = (
            transactions_df.loc[villa_mask, 'merge_key']
            .map(lambda key: villa_groups.get(key, {}))
        )

    # Process Lands
    land_mask = transactions_df['property_type_prop-ai'].isin(['Villa (Land)', 'Land'])

    if land_mask.any() and not land_details.empty:
        # Group land details by merge_key
        land_groups = land_details.groupby('merge_key').apply(
            lambda group: {
                row['building_number']: {
                    'land_type_en': row['land_type_en'], 
                    'parcel_id': row['parcel_id'], 
                    'property_id': row['property_id'],
                    'actual_area': row['actual_area']
                }
                for _, row in group.iterrows()
            }
        ).to_dict()

        # Map land dictionaries to transactions using boolean indexing
        transactions_df.loc[land_mask, 'land_numbers_all'] = (
            transactions_df.loc[land_mask, 'merge_key']
            .map(lambda key: land_groups.get(key, {}))
        )

    def clear_if_multiple_keys(d):
        """Clear dictionary if it contains more than 1 key"""
        return {} if isinstance(d, dict) and len(d) > 1 else d

    def clean_dict(d):
        return {} if not isinstance(d, dict) else d

    transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'] = transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'].apply(clean_dict)
    transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'] = transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'].apply(clean_dict)
    transactions_df['land_numbers_all'] = transactions_df['land_numbers_all'].apply(clean_dict)

    # Apply clear_if_multiple_keys to create the final columns
    transactions_df['unit_numbers'] = transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'].apply(clear_if_multiple_keys)
    transactions_df['villa_numbers'] = transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'].apply(clear_if_multiple_keys)
    transactions_df['land_numbers'] = transactions_df['land_numbers_all'].apply(clear_if_multiple_keys)

    # Clean up temporary columns
    transactions_df.drop(['project_number_numeric', 'merge_key'], axis=1, inplace=True, errors='ignore')

    logger.info("Project dictionaries created successfully")

    return transactions_df

def merge_properties_and_service_charges(transactions_df, mortgages_df, properties_df, charges_df):
    """
    Merge transaction and mortgage data with property and service charge information.

    Performs multi-step merging:
    1. Merges transactions with property details.
    2. Merges with service charges using property group ID and property usage.
    3. Falls back to merging on project number for unmatched records.
    4. Further fallback merging on prop-ai location key building for remaining unmatched.

    Args:
        transactions_df (pandas.DataFrame): Transactions data.
        mortgages_df (pandas.DataFrame): Mortgages data.
        properties_df (pandas.DataFrame): Properties details data.
        charges_df (pandas.DataFrame): Service charges data.

    Returns:
        tuple: (transactions_final, mortgages_final) DataFrames after merges.

    Logs:
        Progress of merging steps, number of duplicates removed,
        number of successful fallback merges, and final merge summary.
    """
    logger.info("Merging additional data sources")

    # Clean MongoDB _id fields
    for df in [mortgages_df, charges_df, properties_df]:
        df.drop(columns=['_id'], inplace=True, errors='ignore')

    def merge_properties_and_charges(df):
        # Properties fields
        props_fields = [
            "transaction_id", "transaction_size", "transaction_date", "transaction_amount",
            "sale_type_id", 
            # "property_id", 
            "property_group_id", "property_usage_id_dld",
            "property_usage_en_dld", "building_name_en_dld"
        ]

        # Drop overlapping fields except transaction_id
        columns_to_drop = [col for col in props_fields if col != "transaction_id" and col in df.columns]

def process_mortgage_data(transactions_df, mortgages_df):
    """
    Match and enrich transactions with mortgage information.

    Matches mortgage records to transactions based primarily on property_id and instance_date,
    allowing a ±120-day window for matching. For transactions missing property_id, uses a fallback
    matching strategy based on a composite key of property attributes.

    Args:
        transactions_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of property transactions.
        mortgages_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of mortgage records.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: transactions_df enriched with mortgage-related columns:
            - 'mortgage_transaction_id'
            - 'mortgage' (Yes/No)
            - 'mortgage_amount'
            - 'mortgage_percent' (mortgage_amount / actual_worth)
            - 'mortgage_type'
            - 'mortgage_type_id'

    Logs:
        Info about the start and successful completion of mortgage data processing.
    """
    logger.info("Processing mortgage data")

    # Convert dates
    transactions_df["instance_date"] = pd.to_datetime(transactions_df["instance_date"])
    mortgages_df["instance_date"] = pd.to_datetime(mortgages_df["instance_date"])

    # Filter mortgages to matching property IDs (for non-NA property_id cases)
    unique_property_ids = transactions_df["property_id"].dropna().unique()
    mortgages_filtered = mortgages_df[mortgages_df["property_id"].isin(unique_property_ids)]

    # Group mortgages by property_id
    mortgage_groups = mortgages_filtered.groupby("property_id")

    # For NA property_id cases, group mortgages by the mapping columns
    mapping_columns = ["property_type_prop-ai", "Number of Bedrooms", "prop-ai_location_key_building", "procedure_area"]

    # Create a composite key for mapping when property_id is NA
    def create_mapping_key(row):
        return tuple(row[col] for col in mapping_columns if col in row.index)

    # Group mortgages by mapping columns for NA property_id matching
    mortgages_na_mapping = {}
    for idx, mortgage in mortgages_df.iterrows():
        if pd.isna(mortgage.get("property_id")):
            key = create_mapping_key(mortgage)
            if key not in mortgages_na_mapping:
                mortgages_na_mapping[key] = []
            mortgages_na_mapping[key].append(mortgage)

    results = []
    for idx, transaction in tqdm(transactions_df.iterrows(), desc="Processing mortgage matches"):
        property_id = transaction["property_id"]
        transaction_id = transaction["transaction_id"]
        actual_worth = transaction.get("actual_worth", None)

        txn_date = transaction["instance_date"]

        mortgage_status = "No"
        mortgage_amount = mortgage_percent = mortgage_type = mortgage_type_id = None

        mortgage_transaction_id = None

        # Check if property_id is available and not NA
        if pd.notna(property_id) and property_id in mortgage_groups.groups:
            related_mortgages = mortgage_groups.get_group(property_id)

            # Filter by ±120 days
            date_range = (
                (related_mortgages["instance_date"] >= txn_date - timedelta(days=120)) & 
                (related_mortgages["instance_date"] <= txn_date + timedelta(days=120))
            )
            filtered = related_mortgages[date_range]

            if not filtered.empty:
                # Find closest match
                filtered = filtered.assign(date_diff=(filtered["instance_date"] - txn_date).abs())
                best_match = filtered.sort_values("date_diff").iloc[0]

                mortgage_transaction_id = best_match.get("transaction_id", None)
                mortgage_status = "Yes"
                mortgage_amount = best_match.get("actual_worth", 0)
                mortgage_percent = mortgage_amount / actual_worth if actual_worth else 0
                mortgage_type = "Mortgage Registration"
                mortgage_type_id = 13

        # If property_id is NA, try mapping on the specified columns
        elif pd.isna(property_id):
            mapping_key = create_mapping_key(transaction)

            if mapping_key in mortgages_na_mapping:
                related_mortgages_list = mortgages_na_mapping[mapping_key]
                related_mortgages = pd.DataFrame(related_mortgages_list)

                # Filter by ±120 days
                date_range = (
                    (related_mortgages["instance_date"] >= txn_date - timedelta(days=120)) & 
                    (related_mortgages["instance_date"] <= txn_date + timedelta(days=120))
                )
                filtered = related_mortgages[date_range]

                if not filtered.empty:
                    # Find closest match
                    filtered = filtered.assign(date_diff=(filtered["instance_date"] - txn_date).abs())
                    best_match = filtered.sort_values("date_diff").iloc[0]

                    mortgage_transaction_id = best_match.get("transaction_id", None)
                    mortgage_status = "Yes"
                    mortgage_amount = best_match.get("actual_worth", 0)
                    mortgage_percent = mortgage_amount / actual_worth if actual_worth else 0
                    mortgage_type = "Mortgage Registration"
                    mortgage_type_id = 13



        results.append({
            "transaction_id": transaction_id,
            "property_id": property_id,
            "mortgage_transaction_id": mortgage_transaction_id,
            "mortgage": mortgage_status,
            "mortgage_amount": mortgage_amount,
            "mortgage_percent": mortgage_percent,
            "mortgage_type": mortgage_type,
            "mortgage_type_id": mortgage_type_id
        })

    mortgage_results_df = pd.DataFrame(results)

    # Merge mortgage results back to transactions
    transactions_df = pd.merge(
        transactions_df, mortgage_results_df, 
        left_on="_id", right_on="transaction_id", 
        how="left", suffixes=('', '_mortgage')
    )

    # Clean up duplicate columns
    transactions_df.drop(['property_id_mortgage', 'transaction_id_mortgage', '_id'], axis=1, inplace=True, errors='ignore')

    logger.info("Mortgage data processing completed")
    return transactions_df

def save_to_mongodb(df, collection, chunk_size=10000):
    """
    Save a DataFrame to a MongoDB collection using a temporary collection for atomic replacement.

    Args:
        df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame to save.
        collection (pymongo.collection.Collection): Target MongoDB collection.
        chunk_size (int): Number of records per insert chunk.

    Raises:
        Exception: Propagates any insertion or rename errors.
    """
    logger.info(f"Saving {len(df)} records to {collection.name}")

    # Get database and create temporary collection name
    db = collection.database
    temp_collection_name = f"{collection.name}_temp"
    temp_collection = db[temp_collection_name]

    df = df.drop(columns=["_id"], errors='ignore')

    def dataframe_to_chunks(df, chunk_size):
        total_rows = len(df)
        for i in range(0, total_rows, chunk_size):
            chunk_df = df.iloc[i:i + chunk_size]
            chunk_records = []

            for record in chunk_df.to_dict('records'):
                for key, value in record.items():
                    if not isinstance(value, (list, dict)) and pd.isnull(value):
                        record[key] = None
                chunk_records.append(record)

            yield chunk_records

    try:
        # Step 1: Drop temporary collection if it exists
        temp_collection.drop()
        logger.info(f"Dropped existing temporary collection: {temp_collection_name}")

        # Step 2: Insert data into temporary collection
        for i, chunk in enumerate(dataframe_to_chunks(df, chunk_size), start=1):
            try:
                temp_collection.insert_many(chunk, ordered=False)
                logger.info(f"✅ Inserted chunk {i} ({len(chunk)} records) to temp collection")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"❌ Error inserting chunk {i} to temp collection: {e}")
                raise

        # Step 3: Rename collections (atomic operation)
        # First rename original collection to backup (if it exists)
        original_exists = collection.name in db.list_collection_names()
        backup_name = f"{collection.name}_backup"

        if original_exists:
            db[collection.name].rename(backup_name)
            logger.info(f"Renamed {collection.name} to {backup_name}")

        # Rename temp collection to target name
        temp_collection.rename(collection.name)
        logger.info(f"Renamed {temp_collection_name} to {collection.name}")

        # Step 4: Drop backup collection
        if original_exists:
            db[backup_name].drop()
            logger.info(f"Dropped backup collection: {backup_name}")

        logger.info(f"✅ Successfully saved {len(df)} records to {collection.name}")

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"❌ Error during save operation: {e}")
        # Cleanup: try to restore from backup if rename was successful
        try:
            if original_exists and backup_name in db.list_collection_names():
                db[backup_name].rename(collection.name)
                logger.info(f"Restored {collection.name} from backup")
        except Exception as restore_error:
            logger.error(f"❌ Error restoring from backup: {restore_error}")

        # Drop temp collection if it still exists
        try:
            if temp_collection_name in db.list_collection_names():
                temp_collection.drop()
                logger.info(f"Cleaned up temporary collection: {temp_collection_name}")
        except Exception as cleanup_error:
            logger.error(f"❌ Error cleaning up temp collection: {cleanup_error}")

        raise

                return "Villa (Land)"
            else:
                return "Land"

        return type_en

def calculate_resale_metrics(transactions_df):
    """
    Calculate resale metrics for property transactions.

    This includes calculating:
    - Number of times a property was sold.
    - Price change relative to the last sale.
    - Price change relative to the first sale of the property.

    Args:
        transactions_df (pandas.DataFrame): DataFrame containing property transaction records.

    Returns:
        pandas.DataFrame: Transactions DataFrame enriched with resale metrics.

    Logs:
        Number of CPU cores used for parallel processing.
        Progress of resale metrics calculation.
        Completion confirmation.
    """
    logger.info("Calculating resale metrics")

    # Preprocess
    transactions_df["instance_date"] = pd.to_datetime(transactions_df["instance_date"])
    transactions_df = transactions_df.sort_values(['property_id', 'instance_date']).reset_index(drop=True)

    def calculate_metrics_single_group(group):
        group = group.sort_values('instance_date').copy()
        group['number_times_sold'] = range(1, len(group) + 1)
        group['last_worth'] = group['actual_worth'].shift(1)
        group['price_change_vs_last_sale'] = (
            (group['actual_worth'] / group['last_worth']) - 1
        ).where(group['last_worth'].notna() & (group['last_worth'] != 0))

        try:
            first_worth = group.loc[group['sale_type_id'] == 1, 'actual_worth'].iloc[0]
            if first_worth != 0:
                group['price_change_vs_first_sale'] = (group['actual_worth'] / first_worth) - 1
            else:
                group['price_change_vs_first_sale'] = pd.NA
        except IndexError:
            group['price_change_vs_first_sale'] = pd.NA

        return group.drop(columns='last_worth')

    # Parallel processing
    grouped = list(transactions_df.groupby('property_id'))
    num_cores = multiprocessing.cpu_count()
    logger.info(f"Processing resale metrics with {num_cores} cores")

    results = Parallel(n_jobs=num_cores)(
        delayed(calculate_metrics_single_group)(group) 
        for _, group in tqdm(grouped, desc="Processing resale metrics")
    )

    # Batch concatenation
    batch_size = 2000
    batches = []
    for i in tqdm(range(0, len(results), batch_size), desc="Concatenating batches"):
        batch = pd.concat(results[i:i + batch_size], ignore_index=True)
        batches.append(batch)

    final_df = pd.concat(batches, ignore_index=True)
    logger.info("Resale metrics calculation completed")
    return final_df

def create_units_and_villas(transactions_df, property_details_df):
    """
    Create dictionaries of units, villas, and lands for each transaction in the dataset.

    This function matches transactions with property details based on composite keys formed
    from project number, area, rooms, and property subtype. It separates properties into units,
    villas, and lands, and aggregates their relevant details into dictionaries attached to each transaction.

    Args:
        transactions_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of property transactions.
        property_details_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame with detailed property attributes.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: transactions_df enriched with columns:
            - 'unit_numbers'
            - 'villa_numbers'
            - 'land_numbers'
        Each containing a dictionary of relevant property details keyed by unit/building number.

    Logs:
        Info on the creation process start and successful completion.
    """
    logger.info("Creating project dictionaries")

    # Ensure unique indices to avoid reindexing errors
    transactions_df = transactions_df.reset_index(drop=True)

    property_details_df = property_details_df[~property_details_df["project_number"].isna()]

    # Convert to numeric once
    transactions_df['project_number_numeric'] = pd.to_numeric(transactions_df['project_number'], errors='coerce')
    property_details_df['project_number_numeric'] = pd.to_numeric(property_details_df['project_number'], errors='coerce')

    # Create merge keys for efficient joining
    transactions_df['merge_key'] = (
        transactions_df['project_number_numeric'].astype(str) + '_' +
        transactions_df['procedure_area'].astype(str) + '_' +
        transactions_df['rooms_en'].astype(str) + '_' +
        transactions_df['property_sub_type_en'].astype(str)
    )

    property_details_df['merge_key'] = (
        property_details_df['project_number_numeric'].astype(str) + '_' +
        property_details_df['actual_area'].astype(str) + '_' +
        property_details_df['rooms_en'].astype(str) + '_' +
        property_details_df['property_sub_type_en'].astype(str)
    )

    # Initialize result columns
    transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'] = [{}] * len(transactions_df)
    transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'] = [{}] * len(transactions_df)
    transactions_df['land_numbers_all'] = [{}] * len(transactions_df)

    # Separate property details by source type for efficiency
    unit_details = property_details_df[property_details_df['Source_Data'] == 'dld_units'].copy()
    land_details = property_details_df[property_details_df['Source_Data'] == 'dld_lands'].copy()

    # Process Units (Apartments & Hotel Apartments)
    apartment_mask = transactions_df['property_type_prop-ai'].isin(['Apartment', 'Hotel Apartment'])

    if apartment_mask.any() and not unit_details.empty:
        # Group unit details by merge_key
        unit_groups = unit_details.groupby('merge_key').apply(
            lambda group: {
                row['unit_number']: {
                    'floor': row['floor'],
                    'unit_balcony_area': row['unit_balcony_area'],
                    'unit_parking_number': row['unit_parking_number'], 
                    'rooms': row['rooms'],
                    'rooms_en': row['rooms_en'], 
                    'building_number': row['building_number'],
                    'property_type_en': row['property_type_en'], 
                    'property_sub_type_en': row['property_sub_type_en'],
                    'land_type_en': row['land_type_en'], 
                    'parcel_id': row['parcel_id'], 
                    'property_id': row['property_id']
                }
                for _, row in group.iterrows()
            }
        ).to_dict()

        # Map unit dictionaries to transactions using boolean indexing
        transactions_df.loc[apartment_mask, 'unit_numbers_all'] = (
            transactions_df.loc[apartment_mask, 'merge_key']
            .map(lambda key: unit_groups.get(key, {}))
        )

    # Process Villas
    villa_mask = transactions_df['property_type_prop-ai'] == 'Villa'

    if villa_mask.any() and not unit_details.empty:
        # Group villa details by merge_key
        villa_groups = unit_details.groupby('merge_key').apply(
            lambda group: {
                row['building_number']: {
                    'built_up_area': row['built_up_area'], 
                    'car_parks': row['car_parks'],
                    'rooms': row['rooms'], 
                    'rooms_en': row['rooms_en'], 
                    'floors': row['floors'],
                    'property_type_en': row['property_type_en'], 
                    'property_sub_type_en': row['property_sub_type_en'],
                    'land_type_en': row['land_type_en'], 
                    'parcel_id': row['parcel_id'], 
                    'property_id': row['property_id']
                }
                for _, row in group.iterrows()
            }
        ).to_dict()

        # Map villa dictionaries to transactions using boolean indexing
        transactions_df.loc[villa_mask, 'villa_numbers_all'] = (
            transactions_df.loc[villa_mask, 'merge_key']
            .map(lambda key: villa_groups.get(key, {}))
        )

    # Process Lands
    land_mask = transactions_df['property_type_prop-ai'].isin(['Villa (Land)', 'Land'])

    if land_mask.any() and not land_details.empty:
        # Group land details by merge_key
        land_groups = land_details.groupby('merge_key').apply(
            lambda group: {
                row['building_number']: {
                    'land_type_en': row['land_type_en'], 
                    'parcel_id': row['parcel_id'], 
                    'property_id': row['property_id'],
                    'actual_area': row['actual_area']
                }
                for _, row in group.iterrows()
            }
        ).to_dict()

        # Map land dictionaries to transactions using boolean indexing
        transactions_df.loc[land_mask, 'land_numbers_all'] = (
            transactions_df.loc[land_mask, 'merge_key']
            .map(lambda key: land_groups.get(key, {}))
        )

    def clear_if_multiple_keys(d):
        """Clear dictionary if it contains more than 1 key"""
        return {} if isinstance(d, dict) and len(d) > 1 else d

    def clean_dict(d):
        return {} if not isinstance(d, dict) else d

    transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'] = transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'].apply(clean_dict)
    transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'] = transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'].apply(clean_dict)
    transactions_df['land_numbers_all'] = transactions_df['land_numbers_all'].apply(clean_dict)

    # Apply clear_if_multiple_keys to create the final columns
    transactions_df['unit_numbers'] = transactions_df['unit_numbers_all'].apply(clear_if_multiple_keys)
    transactions_df['villa_numbers'] = transactions_df['villa_numbers_all'].apply(clear_if_multiple_keys)
    transactions_df['land_numbers'] = transactions_df['land_numbers_all'].apply(clear_if_multiple_keys)

    # Clean up temporary columns
    transactions_df.drop(['project_number_numeric', 'merge_key'], axis=1, inplace=True, errors='ignore')

    logger.info("Project dictionaries created successfully")

    return transactions_df

    """

def merge_properties_and_service_charges(transactions_df, mortgages_df, properties_df, charges_df):
    """
    Merge transaction and mortgage data with property and service charge information.

    Performs multi-step merging:
    1. Merges transactions with property details.
    2. Merges with service charges using property group ID and property usage.
    3. Falls back to merging on project number for unmatched records.
    4. Further fallback merging on prop-ai location key building for remaining unmatched.

    Args:
        transactions_df (pandas.DataFrame): Transactions data.
        mortgages_df (pandas.DataFrame): Mortgages data.
        properties_df (pandas.DataFrame): Properties details data.
        charges_df (pandas.DataFrame): Service charges data.

    Returns:
        tuple: (transactions_final, mortgages_final) DataFrames after merges.

    Logs:
        Progress of merging steps, number of duplicates removed,
        number of successful fallback merges, and final merge summary.
    """
    logger.info("Merging additional data sources")

    # Clean MongoDB _id fields
    for df in [mortgages_df, charges_df, properties_df]:
        df.drop(columns=['_id'], inplace=True, errors='ignore')

    def merge_properties_and_charges(df):
        # Properties fields
        props_fields = [
            "transaction_id", "transaction_size", "transaction_date", "transaction_amount",
            "sale_type_id", 
            # "property_id", 
            "property_group_id", "property_usage_id_dld",
            "property_usage_en_dld", "building_name_en_dld"
        ]

        # Drop overlapping fields except transaction_id
        columns_to_drop = [col for col in props_fields if col != "transaction_id" and col in df.columns]
        df_cleaned = df.drop(columns=columns_to_drop)

        # Merge properties
        props_trimmed = properties_df[props_fields].drop_duplicates(subset=['transaction_id'])
        df_merged = pd.merge(df_cleaned, props_trimmed, on="transaction_id", how="left")

        # Service charges fields
        charges_fields = [
            "master_project_id", "property_group_name_en", "service_charge_group_name_en",
            "property_group_id", "service_charges_budget_year", "service_charge_group_usage_en",
            "service_charges_general_fund", "service_charges_total"
        ]

        # Drop overlapping charges fields except property_group_id
        columns_to_drop = [col for col in charges_fields if col != "property_group_id" and col in df_merged.columns]
        df_merged_cleaned = df_merged.drop(columns=columns_to_drop)

        # Step 1: Primary merge using property_group_id
        charges_trimmed = charges_df[charges_fields].drop_duplicates(subset=['property_group_id', 'service_charge_group_usage_en'])
        df_with_charges = pd.merge(
            df_merged_cleaned,
            charges_trimmed,
            left_on=["property_group_id", "property_usage_en_dld"],
            right_on=["property_group_id", "service_charge_group_usage_en"],
            how="left"
        )

        display(df_with_charges)

        # Step 2: Fallback merge using project_number
        no_charges_mask = df_with_charges['service_charges_total'].isna()

        if no_charges_mask.sum() > 0 and "project_number" in charges_df.columns:
            logger.info(f"Step 2: Attempting project_number fallback merge for {no_charges_mask.sum()} records")

            # Prepare project_number fallback merge
            project_fallback_fields = [
                "project_number", "service_charge_group_name_en", "service_charges_budget_year", 
                "service_charge_group_usage_en", "service_charges_general_fund", "service_charges_total"
            ]
            available_project_fields = [field for field in project_fallback_fields if field in charges_df.columns]

            # Create project_number charges dataset
            charges_project = charges_df[available_project_fields].copy()

            # Remove rows where project_number is NaN
            charges_project = charges_project.dropna(subset=["project_number"])
            duplicate_mask = charges_project.duplicated(subset=["project_number"], keep=False)
            charges_project_unique = charges_project[~duplicate_mask]

            # Remove duplicates - if multiple matches exist, ignore them
            duplicate_mask = charges_project.duplicated(subset=["project_number"], keep=False)
            charges_project_unique = charges_project[~duplicate_mask]

            logger.info(f"Removed {duplicate_mask.sum()} duplicate project_number records")

            # Get records that need fallback merge
            df_no_charges = df_with_charges[no_charges_mask].copy()

            # Perform project_number fallback merge
            df_project_merged = pd.merge(
                df_no_charges.drop(columns=[col for col in charges_fields[1:] if col in df_no_charges.columns]),
                charges_project_unique,
                on="project_number",
                how="left"
            )

            # Update main dataframe with project_number results
            project_success_mask = ~df_project_merged['service_charges_total'].isna()
            update_indices = df_with_charges.index[no_charges_mask][project_success_mask]

            for col in charges_project_unique.columns:
                if col != "project_number":
                    df_with_charges.loc[update_indices, col] = df_project_merged.loc[project_success_mask, col].values

            project_success_count = project_success_mask.sum()
            logger.info(f"Project_number merge successful for {project_success_count} records")

        # Step 3: Fallback merge using prop-ai_location_key_building
        no_charges_mask = df_with_charges['service_charges_total'].isna()

        if no_charges_mask.sum() > 0 and "prop-ai_location_key_building" in charges_df.columns:
            logger.info(f"Step 3: Attempting prop-ai_location_key_building fallback merge for {no_charges_mask.sum()} records")

            # Prepare location key fallback merge  
            location_fallback_fields = [
                "prop-ai_location_key_building", "service_charge_group_name_en", "service_charges_budget_year",
                "service_charge_group_usage_en", "service_charges_general_fund", "service_charges_total"
            ]
            available_location_fields = [field for field in location_fallback_fields if field in charges_df.columns]

            # Create location key charges dataset
            charges_location = charges_df[available_location_fields].copy()

            # charges_location = charges_location.copy()

            # Remove duplicates - if multiple matches exist, ignore them
            charges_location = charges_location[~(charges_location["prop-ai_location_key_building"] == '')]
            charges_location = charges_location[~charges_location.isna()]
            charges_location_unique = charges_location.drop_duplicates(subset=["prop-ai_location_key_building"])

            logger.info(f"Removed {duplicate_mask.sum()} duplicate prop-ai_location_key_building records")

            # Get records that still need fallback merge
            df_still_no_charges = df_with_charges[no_charges_mask].copy()

            # Perform location key fallback merge
            df_location_merged = pd.merge(
                df_still_no_charges.drop(columns=[col for col in charges_fields[1:] if col in df_still_no_charges.columns]),
                charges_location_unique,
                on="prop-ai_location_key_building",
                how="left"
            )

            # Update main dataframe with location key results
            location_success_mask = ~df_location_merged['service_charges_total'].isna()
            update_indices = df_with_charges.index[no_charges_mask][location_success_mask]

            for col in charges_location_unique.columns:
                if col != "prop-ai_location_key_building":
                    df_with_charges.loc[update_indices, col] = df_location_merged.loc[location_success_mask, col].values

            location_success_count = location_success_mask.sum()
            logger.info(f"Location key merge successful for {location_success_count} records")

        # Final summary
        final_no_charges = df_with_charges['service_charges_total'].isna().sum()
        total_records = len(df_with_charges)
        logger.info(f"Final merge summary: {total_records - final_no_charges}/{total_records} records have service charges")

        return df_with_charges

    transactions_final = merge_properties_and_charges(transactions_df)
    mortgages_final = merge_properties_and_charges(mortgages_df)

    logger.info("Additional data merged successfully")
    return transactions_final, mortgages_final
